style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A prayer against the silence of God. David calls to his Rock and asks Him not to be deaf, because an unanswering God would leave him indistinguishable from the men going down to the pit. He lifts his hands toward the inner sanctuary and asks two things: not to be dragged off with the wicked -- defined here not by violence but by duplicity, peace on their lips and evil in their hearts -- and that those men receive exactly what their own hands made, since they pay no attention to what God's hands have made. Then, between one verse and the next, the silence breaks. Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard -- the very words of the request, now a fact -- and the psalm runs through the four beats of an answered prayer: my heart trusted, I was helped, my heart exults, I will thank Him with my song. It ends by widening from the king to the people: the LORD is their strength and the stronghold of His anointed; save Your people, bless Your inheritance, shepherd them and carry them forever. The Te Deum has carried that last verse for fifteen hundred years.

1.text: Of David. To You, O LORD, I call; my Rock, do not turn a deaf ear to me -- for if You keep silent toward me, I will become like those who go down to the pit.
1.amp: A Psalm of David. Unto You will I cry [qara], O LORD [YHWH] my rock [tsur]; be not silent ['from me', chashah, the KJV margin] to me: lest, if You be silent [charash -- deaf] to me, I become [mashal -- be likened] like them that go down [yarad] into the pit [bor].
1.notes: elekha YHWH eqra tsuri al-techerash mimmenni (H3068, H7121, H6697, H2790): to You I call, my Rock -- do not be deaf 'from me', the margin's literal; pen-techesheh mimmenni (H2814): lest You be silent -- ve-nimshalti im-yorde bor (H4911, H3381, H953): and I be made like the pit-descenders. Two different silence-verbs in one verse: the prayer's whole terror is an unanswering God (cf. Psalm 143:7).

2.text: Hear the voice of my pleas for grace when I cry to You for help, when I lift my hands toward Your Most Holy Place.
2.amp: Hear [shama] the voice [qol] of my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace], when I cry [shava] unto You, when I lift up [nasa] my hands [yad] toward Your holy [qodesh] oracle ['the oracle of thy sanctuary', qodesh, the KJV margin].
2.notes: shema qol tachanunai be-shavvei elekha (H8085, H6963, H8469, H7768): hear the voice of my grace-pleas when I SHOUT to You -- be-nosi yadai el-debir qodshekha (H5375, H3027, H1687, H6944): lifting my hands toward the debir of Your holiness -- the inner room, the Holy of Holies, the margin's 'oracle'. Prayer aimed at a place because the ark, and the mercy seat, were there (cf. 1 Kings 8:29-30).

3.text: Do not drag me off with the wicked, with the workers of iniquity, who speak peace to their neighbors while evil is in their hearts.
3.amp: Draw me not away [mashak -- drag] with the wicked [rasha], and with the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven], which speak [dabar] peace [shalom] to their neighbours [rea], but mischief [ra -- evil] is in their hearts [lebab].
3.notes: al-timshekheni im-reshaim (H4900, H7563): do not DRAG me off with the wicked -- Psalm 26:9's fear in a rougher verb -- ve-im-poale aven (H6466, H205): with the workers of wickedness -- dobere shalom im-reehem ve-raah bi-lebabam (H1696, H7965, H7453, H7451, H3824): who say shalom to their neighbors with evil in their hearts. The definition of the wicked here is not violence but duplicity: peace on the lips, evil in the heart (cf. Jeremiah 9:8).

4.text: Give them according to their deeds and the evil of their practices; give them what the work of their hands deserves; pay them back what they have earned.
4.amp: Give [natan] them according to their deeds [poal], and according to the wickedness [roa] of their endeavours: give [natan] them after the work [maaseh] of their hands [yad]; render [shub -- return] to them their desert [gemul -- recompense].
4.notes: ten-lahem ke-phoolam u-khe-roa maalelehem (H5414, H6467, H7455, H4611): give them by their deeds and by the evil of their practices -- ke-maaseh yedehem ten lahem (H4639, H3027, H5414): by the work of their hands -- hasheb gemulam lahem (H7725, H1576): RETURN their recompense to them. Four clauses asking for one thing: that the wicked receive exactly what they made -- Psalm 9:15's justice as a petition. Nothing extra is asked, only the accurate.

5.text: Because they pay no attention to the deeds of the LORD or the work of His hands, He will tear them down and never build them up.
5.amp: Because they regard [bin -- discern] not the works [peullah] of the LORD [YHWH], nor the operation [maaseh -- work] of His hands [yad], He shall destroy [haras -- tear down] them, and not build them up [banah].
5.notes: ki lo yabinu el-peullot YHWH ve-el-maaseh yadav (H995, H6468, H3068, H4639, H3027): because they do not DISCERN the LORD's deeds and the work of His hands -- the wicked man's inattention (Psalm 10:4) is his indictment -- yeheresem ve-lo yibnem (H2040, H1129): He will tear them down and not build them up, Jeremiah's pair of verbs (Jeremiah 1:10) running one direction. The 'work of hands' of verse 4 and of verse 5 are set against each other: theirs and His.

6.text: Blessed be the LORD! He has heard the voice of my pleading for grace.
6.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH], because He has heard [shama] the voice [qol] of my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace].
6.notes: barukh YHWH ki-shama qol tachanunai (H1288, H3068, H8085, H6963, H8469): blessed be the LORD -- He HAS heard the voice of my pleas: verse 2's request repeated word for word as a fact. Between verse 5 and verse 6 something happened that the psalm does not narrate -- the silence of verse 1 broke -- and the lament becomes a thanksgiving mid-page, as Psalm 6:8-9 does.

7.text: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in Him, and I was helped; so my heart leaps for joy, and with my song I will thank Him.
7.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is my strength [oz] and my shield [magen]; my heart [leb] trusted [batach] in Him, and I am helped [azar]: therefore my heart [leb] greatly rejoices [alaz -- exults]; and with my song [shir] will I praise [yadah -- thank] Him.
7.notes: YHWH uzzi u-maginni (H3068, H5797, H4043): my strength and my shield -- the paired titles of Psalm 18:2, where He is 'my rock' and 'my shield' -- bo batach libbi ve-neezarti (H982, H3820, H5826): in Him my heart trusted and I WAS HELPED -- va-yaaloz libbi u-mi-shiri ahodennu (H5937, H7892, H3034): so my heart exults, and from my song I will thank Him. Trust, help, joy, song: the four beats of an answered prayer, in order.

8.text: The LORD is strength for His people; He is a stronghold of salvation for His anointed.
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is their ['his', oz, the KJV margin] strength [oz], and He is the saving ['strength of salvations', yeshuah, the KJV margin] strength [maoz -- stronghold] of His anointed [mashiach].
8.notes: YHWH oz-lamo (H3068, H5797): the LORD is strength 'to them' -- or, as the margin and many manuscripts read, 'to His people'; u-maoz yeshuot meshicho hu (H4581, H3444, H4899): and He is the stronghold of salvations -- the margin's plural -- of His mashiach, His anointed. The individual thanksgiving widens: the king's rescue is the nation's strength, which is what an anointed king is for -- and why the church reads verse 8 of the Anointed One.

9.text: Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.
9.amp: Save [yasha] Your people [am], and bless [barak] Your inheritance [nachalah]: feed ['rule', raah, the KJV margin] them also, and lift them up [nasa -- carry] for ever [olam].
9.notes: hoshiah et-ammekha u-barekh et-nachalatekha (H3467, H5971, H1288, H5159): save Your people, bless Your inheritance -- u-reem ve-nasseem ad-ha-olam (H7462, H5375, H5769): SHEPHERD them -- raah, which the margin renders 'rule', the shepherd-king's verb -- and CARRY them forever, nasa, the verb of Isaiah 40:11's lambs and Deuteronomy 1:31's father. The psalm that began afraid of God's silence ends asking Him to pick the whole flock up. The Te Deum's 'O Lord, save thy people, and bless thine heritage' is this verse.
